title: Arjun Mehta KV + quant scratchlog (daily)
content:
Quick purpose
- scratchpad for small, messy notes: KV cache experiments + quantization variants + short prompts to retest. Not polished. Use links above for canonical results.

Open questions / hypotheses
- Can int4 quant with per-block outlier compensation keep decode quality for chat prompts with long histories? Hypothesis: if we only quantize weights for attention matmul and keep layernorm/softmax in fp16, loss/PI will be within 1–2%.
- Does increasing KV cache shard size reduce latency variance for long context (8k tokens) on A100s? Expect small improvement but higher memory tail.

Today's TODO (short)
- [ ] Re-run run-042 with seed 42 + topk=40 (Maya asked for larger topk)
- [ ] Add a small eval harness that uses 1k real chat histories (from sample set) to measure hallucination rate post-quant
- [ ] Push small README to PR 2345 explaining the bench harness and how to reproduce

Experiment log (lightweight)
- run-042 (2026-03-10)
  model: redwood/llama2-13b-v1 (baseline fp16)
  config: batch=8, seq=2048, kv_shard=4, quant=None
  notes: baseline latency P50=86ms/token, P95=210ms/token (on p3a.8x), avg memory 19.8GB
  eval quick: Rouge-L on prompt-set-A = 0.78, LL drop vs ref = 0.0 (baseline)

- run-043 (2026-03-11) int8 static quant (per-tensor)
  model: same
  config: batch=8, seq=2048, kv_shard=4, quant=int8, keep-layernorm-fp16
  notes: P50=72ms/token, P95=190ms/token, mem 13.6GB
  quality: Rouge-L 0.76, occasional short-token truncation in examples with many newlines (investigate tokenization/attention handling)
  conclusion: good perf lift, minor quality regression on some prompt types (code blocks)

- run-044 (2026-03-12) int4 per-block (outlier compensation enabled)
  config: batch=4, seq=4096, kv_shard=2, quant=int4-perblock, outlier-threshold=0.02
  notes: P50=68ms/token, P95=240ms/token (variance high), mem 9.8GB
  quality: Rouge-L 0.74, more hallucination on longer prompts (context bleeding). suspect accumulation error in KV when quantized below 8-bit.

Quick commands used (for my future self)
- run locally: ./bench/run_eval.sh --model redwood/llama2-13b-v1 --quant int8 --batch 8 --seq 2048 --kv-shards 4 --seed 42
- profile: python tools/profile_latency.py --trace --out run-043-trace.json
- dump weights: python tools/dump_block_stats.py --model-dir /mnt/models/llama-13b --out stats-2026-03-11.csv

Observations / heuristics so far
- Keep layernorm & attention softmax in fp16 when trying int4; otherwise numeric instability shows up quickly (especially in long recency prompts).
- KV shard count tradeoff: more shards => lower peak mem but higher P95 due to cross-shard syncs. For dedicated infra with fast NVLink, shard=4 is sweet spot for 13b at seq<=2048.
- Outlier comp helps mean quality but increases P95 latency a lot; tune threshold per-layer rather than global.

Prompts to retest (short list)
- Multi-turn chat (10 turns): prompt-template-multi-turn-v2.txt (explicit role tokens, system prompt removed)
- Code extraction: prompt-code-summarize-v1 (edge-case tokens with long code blocks)
- Retrieval-augmented: rerank prompt w/ 5 docs; test hit-rate when context quantized

Notes to self (messy)
- If re-run fails on p95 latency spike, collect nvprof + dmesg — might be host-level interference (noisy neighbor on shared dev box). Consider using dedicated bench node.
- Talk to infra (Leo) about reserving 1x a100-80gb for a short stability run with seq=8192. Need to verify memory fragmentation when doing warmup micro-batches.

Outstanding followups
- [ ] Add per-layer quant stats to PR 2345 (Maya wants the worst-3-layers callouts)
- [ ] Hook eval harness to alert when Rouge-L delta > 0.03 vs baseline for any prompt set (quality regression watcher)
- [ ] Proposal: add an automatic fallback to int8 for layers flagged as "high-outlier" during compilation. Draft a tiny proposal in /confluence and link it.

Random observations from slack thread #aml-kv (copied)
- Ida: "we saw similar context-bleed with int4 on 30b; layering fp16 LN was critical"
- Maya: "try topk tuning; lower topk sometimes hides truncation artifacts in code-blocks"

End note
- This doc is ephemeral. If something becomes important, move into a proper bench-results doc under shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/benchmarks. For now, keep it noisy.
